__about__: ROADMAP task 4 -- broaden model coverage. This file is the PROVENANCE RECORD for runs that live
in uncommitted scratch: model_sweep.verify_point checks every field below against each run's own
HDF5 metadata and RAISES on mismatch, so a design point whose files say something else is caught
as a staging bug rather than silently averaged in.
Seed ranges are allocated from 2e7 upward at 1e6 per point, disjoint from seed_ensemble's default
1e6 and run_beta_ladder's 2e6 + beta*1e6. Walker streams are hash(global_id + base_seed), so
overlapping ranges would silently make every interval too narrow (Gotcha 13);
validate_manifest refuses to emit commands if any two points overlap.
`model` is the DRIVER name (what plan hands to run_*.sh); `model_label` is what the lattice
writes into the HDF5 as SYMM_VARIANCE_MODEL_LABEL. They differ (square -> square_D4), so the
provenance check is against `model_label` -- checking `model` flagged every square run as
Costs below are MEASURED, not guessed: the calibration constant t(64 ranks x 2048/rank) /
t(16 ranks x 512/rank) = 13.9 was pinned on 2026-07-28 against fe_as's known 125 s at 64x2048
(its scout took 9 s). A 32-seed ensemble is 32x that.

points.label: square_b5_c4
points.role: KEYSTONE -- de-confounds temperature from band count against the FeAs beta=5 headline. Square's committed ladder is at beta in {1,2,4,8}, so beta=5 does not exist yet and without it the nb axis is three unconnected points rather than a trend.

points.label: threeband_b5_c4
__warmup_note__: 8000, NOT the Conventions' 200 -- measured, ROADMAP task 4 gate 3, 2026-07-28.
WHAT IS ESTABLISHED: warm-up 200 is inadequate for this model. At 200 the depth ladder
appears to drift (R = 2.965 at m=2048 -> 3.322 at m=8192, the step resolved in all 3
seeds), which reads as an unconverged depth floor but is not one. Raising warm-up
200 -> 2000 at FIXED m=2048 moves R by +0.407, reproducing the +0.357 that 4x depth
bought. The chain was not thermalized, and extra depth was diluting an unthermalized
prefix rather than curing it. Square at the same beta is flat in depth at warm-up 200,
which is the control making this specific to threeband's much larger expansion order
(U_dd = 8 across 3 bands) rather than a general flaw.
WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: where warm-up converges. 2000 -> 8000 moves R by -0.096 +/- 0.021
-- decelerating hard from +0.407 and with the SIGN REVERSED, which is not the shape smooth
thermalization predicts. Crucially that comparison is n=3 on a model with <s> ~ 0.57, and
Conventions are explicit that three seeds cannot resolve a parameter effect on a
sign-problem model: the FeAs warm-up effect that looked resolved at n=3 (+0.34 +/- 0.13,
3/3 same sign) vanished at 8 seeds. So the 2000-vs-8000 difference is NOT believed here.
DECISION: run the ensemble at the most thermalized point tested (8000) and carry the
warm-up difference as a DISCLOSED SYSTEMATIC, measured at 8 seeds by the sensitivity arm
below rather than asserted at 3. It is ~2.8%, which exceeds the across-seed statistical
error, so it must be quoted alongside R and not buried.

sensitivity_arm.label: threeband_b5_c4_w2000
sensitivity_arm.role: Powers the warm-up systematic to n=8, the minimum Conventions accept on a sign-problem model. Not a headline point.

points.role: The nb=3 point AND the inequivalent-orbital control in one run. Measured band-equivalence classes [[0],[1,2]]: d inequivalent, p_x ~ p_y equivalent, and exactly two realized band permutations (identity and the p_x<->p_y transposition, no d<->p). Requires U_pp = 2 and mu = 3 -- see the template's operating-point note; at U_pp = 0 the p-block G is deterministic and the run measures nothing.

points.label: square_b5_c8
points.role: Cluster-size axis at fixed beta and nb -- the roadmap's open question, does rho fall with Nc? Scouting confirms the geometry claim of TAKEAWAYS 6 directly: orbit sizes go {1:2, 2:1, 4:3} at 4x4 to {1:2, 2:1, 4:9, 8:3} at 8x8, i.e. three FREE m=8 orbits that a 4x4 mesh cannot have. n_seeds cut to 16: at 32 the ensemble is 6.2 h, over the 4 h budget rule.

reference_points.label: fe_as_b5_c4
reference_points.role: Already measured at 32 seeds as the beta=5 rung. Reused, NOT re-run -- re-running would spend 70 minutes reproducing a committed number.

blocked_points.label: kagome_b5_c4
blocked_points.status: BLOCKED -- DCA-side segfault, out of scope
detail: Kagome was the only model in the tree with THREE symmetry-equivalent orbitals and the only
route to a |G| = 12 point group, so it is worth recording precisely why it cannot run.
The target builds (KagomeHubbard<D6> passes orbit_table.hpp's CanDeriveSymmetry
static_assert) but every run segfaults inside DCA's own
i.e. in production's symmetrization of G0, before any driver code runs. gdb backtrace
confirmed. Cause: Kagome's flavors() = {0,1,2} are all distinct, so set_symmetry_matrices'
position+flavor matching cannot place a rotated sublattice and records a band image of -1
(visible as '"P" : [ -1]' in the run log); those -1 images are then dereferenced.
Declaring D4 instead of D6 does NOT help -- also segfaults -- so it is the derive/record
path, not the declared group. DCA's own characterization test reaches 12 derived ops only
by calling verifiedSymmetryOps(H0) directly on a no_symmetry<2> instantiation, which never
Fixing it means patching DCA's symmetrization, which ROADMAP task 4 scopes out. The .cpp and
template are kept so the attempt is not repeated from scratch.
